Lion: Domain Eukarya, kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Mammalia, order Carnivora, family Felidae, genus Panthera, species Panthera leo. Corn: Domain Eukarya, kingdom Plantae, division Magnoliophyta, class Liliopsida, order Poales, family Poaceae, genus Zea, species Zea mays.

The Linnaean system classifies organisms in a hierarchy from broadest to most specific: kingdom, phylum (or division), class, order, family, genus, and species. Each kingdom contains phyla or divisions; each phylum or division contains classes; each class contains orders; each order contains families; each family contains genera; and each genus contains species. Domain is a broader rank above kingdom; the three-domain system was proposed by Carl Woese and colleagues in 1990.

Incorrect classification can lead to misunderstandings about an organism’s relationships and characteristics. This can result in unsuitable conservation decisions and unreliable scientific studies or comparisons.

Study the organism’s characteristics and compare them with known organisms to determine its taxonomic placement and whether it represents a new species. Assign it to a genus, then give it a two-part binomial: the genus name followed by the specific epithet. Capitalize the genus, lowercase the specific epithet, and italicize the full name (or underline it when handwritten).
